scope: Original vfork release and source parent wait, non-last exit with opaque owner controls, asynchronous cold projection collection, original weak mm publication roots and namespace completion dependency ordering. Last/group/default-fatal entry and final CPU/mm custody remain joined.
changes: The actual vfork child publishes its original release after dropping its CPU View, independently of an occupied owner or unrelated peer CPU. Owner exit/exec finish the same object once.

A sole runnable original vfork child admits its actual waiting parent by release-object identity; no unrelated runnable task is required. Pending release preserves stop custody and background ring CQ progress does not complete the wait.

Opaque owner FD kinds no longer refuse an otherwise admitted non-last exit. Logical Files retirement stays on the source; private Rc controls and the Memory wrapper are collected asynchronously on their existing owner.
Original group cleanup membership finishes after cold projection collection. Full Done CPU/metrics still return at cohort drain.

Weak original Memory roots are captured only for actual returned exits. They preserve legacy backing writes when all dispatched wrappers are gone but an undispatched task owns the same mm. No strong keeper retains RAM.
Original Families record status and optional host completion, and release namespace-init dependents only after their original victim families complete, even following ancestor namespace death.

concurrency.synchronization: Original per-group and family graph mutexes; original execution queue and coalesced completion event. Release/acquire only for the actual vfork child/parent completion. Private Rc and weak mm roots stay on their original owner.

mechanism_controls.red: Old ancestor-dead short circuit omits its actual descendant dependency.

checks.native_reference: Existing 6 CPU/8GB ARM Linux test instance. It is stopped during Mac timing and is not a product Linux-kernel VM.

thread_completion_benchmark.scope: 128 two-thread groups: fork, clone, leader exit, final thread exit and parent wait. Half retain ordinary files and half actual owner epoll controls. Both threads exit zero in bench mode so old and new binaries perform identical valid work. Seven counterbalanced pairs per CPU count. No test Linux instance/build was running during timings. Includes joined fork/mm/last-exit work; not a Firefox or general CPU benchmark. Final pinned Mac development binary. Native ARM Linux reference ran the same ELF in the existing 6 CPU/8GB hardware-backed Linux test instance, not native macOS.

vfork_benchmark.scope: Actual vfork child exits while another thread in its group spins; parent release must not await that thread or the whole cohort. Plain and unique legacy epoll controls, eight rounds each, seven after samples; seven counterbalanced baseline pairs for one CPU. Baseline multicore hits the explicit two-second fixture deadline, not a completed latency. No Linux instance or build runs during timing. Native Linux reference is the existing ARM hardware-backed 6 CPU/8GB test instance, not native macOS.

experiments.stopped_cohort_guard: Seven counterbalanced pairs showed no consistent benefit; experiment was removed, with a backup retained in ignored scratch.
experiments.lazy_roots: Seven pairs against first source-completion candidate showed about 1% multicore change; do not claim a broad speedup. Final stock-baseline comparison below remains slower for ordinary thread churn.

remaining: Final Done CPU/metrics adoption and last shared Memory graph/backing publication still use joined cohort completion.
Last-member exit(93), exit_group(94), default-fatal cleanup and source namespace victim termination remain connected work.
Structural clone/exec, robust futex support and actual excluded control operations retain their boundaries.
